long_biography.plain_text:
Marco Testa went to New York in the early 1970s to work at Benton & Bowles and study marketing and brand management, seeking experience beyond his father's celebrated agency. Back in Italy, he founded L'Altra in Milan in 1977. After early setbacks, the business recovered and later merged with Armando Testa, bringing him onto the family group's board; he became chief executive in 1985 and later added the presidency.

His leadership joined inherited creative heritage with an appetite for new formats. The group developed media, branding, production and digital units, opened a Los Angeles operation and formed an automotive communications venture with French agency Herezie. Testa also served two terms as president of Italy's advertising-industry association. He continues to lead the independent group while backing technology-led expansion, including its investment in marketing-technology specialist RedAbissi.
